# @zakkster/lite-map

> Zero-GC keyed list reconciliation for @zakkster/lite-signal: mapArray and
> indexArray that MOVE and REBIND per-item reactive scopes instead of rebuilding
> them, reusing retired scopes from a free-list so steady-state list churn never
> grows the engine pool.

Map a reactive array to one reactive scope per item. List mutation moves and
rebinds scopes; only changed items recompute. The differentiator vs Solid's
mapArray: removed items' scopes go to a free-list and are REUSED by later
inserts, so churn over a bounded set pulls nothing from the pool.

Peer dependency: @zakkster/lite-signal ^1.6.0-preview.0 (uses createScope, the
detached per-item-subtree disposal primitive). ESM only. DOM-free. MIT.

## The fork this ships

By-accessor: the CHANGING dimension is always an accessor. That is what lets a
retired scope be reused for a new item by setting its signals (no rebuild). A
by-value mapArray (item as a plain value) cannot reuse a scope for a new item, so
its inserts pull from the pool -- it is a planned opt-in, NOT in 1.0.

## Entry points

- createMapper(reg) -> { mapArray, indexArray }   // bind to any registry >=1.6.0-preview.0
- mapArray(list, mapFn, opts?)                     // default registry, item-keyed
- indexArray(list, mapFn, opts?)                   // default registry, position-keyed

## indexArray(list, (item, index) => O, { maxPool? })

- POSITION-keyed. `item` is an accessor (the value at this slot); `index` is a
  plain number (the slot is stable).
- Value churn at a stable length = itemSig.set per changed slot. Zero-GC.
- Grow appends; shrink parks tail slots to a LIFO free-pool; tail re-grow reuses a
  parked slot when its index matches (push/pop at the end is zero-GC). A reused
  slot whose index would not match is disposed + rebuilt (keeps the plain `index`
  correct). maxPool caps retained parked slots.

## mapArray(list, (item, index) => O, { key?, maxPool? })

- ITEM-keyed. BOTH `item` and `index` are accessors.
- key: identity selector, default reference identity (the item). Keys must be
  unique within the list.
- Survivor reused in place; if it moved, idxSig.set (zero-GC); if its item changed
  under a stable key, itemSig.set. Removed -> retired to the free-list. New -> a
  retired scope reused via itemSig.set + idxSig.set (zero-GC when the pool is
  warm), else built. maxPool caps retained retired scopes.

## Returned accessor: Mapped<O>

- mapped() -> O[]   the outputs in source order. ONE persistent array, mutated in
  place (zero per-change allocation): read fresh each run; do not retain or
  reference-compare. Fires only on a real structural change (membership/order),
  not on value-only churn.
- mapped.dispose()   stop the driver, dispose every live + parked scope (including
  the item/index signals the scope does not own) and the output signal.

## Ownership

- Each item owns a createScope() scope; its mapFn effects/computeds are cascaded
  on disposal. Per-item scopes AND the reconcile driver are detached from the
  caller (createRoot/createScope), so an enclosing scope re-running never tears
  the list down. The caller owns teardown via mapped.dispose() -- there is no
  auto-cleanup.

## Zero-GC (engine pool counters), and the honest non-claims

PASS (poolGrowths / totalAllocations flat after warm-up, verified):
- indexArray value churn at a stable length (20k updates flat).
- mapArray reorder/move (idxSig.set on shifted survivors).
- mapArray warm-pool insert/remove churn (5k iters flat).
- indexArray tail grow/shrink via the free-pool.
NOT claimed:
- Growth past the previous high-water mark pulls scopes from the pool.
- The keyed byKey Map mutates (set/delete) on actual key changes -- a JS
  allocation the pool counters do not see. Reorder touches no key, so no Map churn.
- The user's mapFn body (its allocations are the caller's).

## Gotchas

- createScope cascades effects/computeds but NOT signals (the engine never
  owner-adopts signals). lite-map disposes the item/index signals it creates. A
  BARE signal you create inside mapFn is NOT auto-disposed on scope teardown --
  prefer effects/computeds (which ARE cascaded), or dispose it yourself.
- Call mapArray/indexArray once at setup; reading the returned accessor is the
  reactive surface. Disposal is explicit (mapped.dispose()).
- Deferred to a later minor: by-value mapArray, LIS minimal-move ordering (1.0
  moves are correct but not minimal), append/pop fast-paths.
